title: Priority Ladder and Intake Flow for Partial-Connectivity Private Deployments (Staged Bridge Pattern)
creator: Maya Patel
description: Create a repeatable intake and prioritization runbook for customers who cannot provide full egress or persistent connectivity but can accept a staged-bridge/proxy for limited windows. This ticket defines the intake form changes, priority ladder (fastpass / standard / concierge), minimum technical acceptance criteria, and escalation lanes. The goal is to reduce engineering review time by 40% on first-touch, provide predictable SLAs for customers on the fastpass lane, and ensure security/compliance guardrails are enforced for partially connected private/VPC/on-prem requests.
acceptance_criteria: Intake form updated to capture staged-bridge capability, allowed egress windows, proxy constraints, and customer-side ops resource availability
Priority ladder documented with clear thresholds (signal score, contract value, regulatory constraints) and SLA targets for each lane
Runbook includes triage checklist for network sniffing, proxy health checks, and fallback sequencing
Template comms for fastpass, standard, and concierge lanes available for solutions engineers
Telemetry events defined so we can measure TTF triage and time-to-onboard for each lane
steps: 1) Update customer intake form: add fields for 'partial egress allowed', 'egress windows (UTC)', 'on-prem proxy present (Y/N)', 'maintenance window SLA' and 'contactable ops during window'
2) Auto-score submission: compute a triage score from connectivity, data sensitivity, regulatory regime, and contract tier to assign lane (fastpass/standard/concierge)
3) Fastpass lane: if score >= 85 and customer provides a vetted bastion/proxy and maintenance window >= 2h, schedule a 2h bridge test in next 72h
4) Standard lane: schedule network readiness call; engineering assessment required if proxy absent or windows < 2h
5) Concierge lane: concierge + eng + security working session; require dedicated runbook and escalation points
6) During test window: run automated probe suite (port checks, TLS handshake, throughput, latency, and KV cache smoke) and validate telemetry emission
7) Post-test: generate onboarding report and required config changes for long-term deployment; if test fails, follow rollback and remediation lanes
8) Close loop: record triage metrics, customer impact tags, and update intake scoring model based on outcomes
notes: This runbook intentionally separates partial-connectivity from full-airgap requests. It prioritizes a reproducible staged-bridge test that exercises the minimum path for inference (model pull, KV warm, short-run inference) rather than a full production cutover. Trade-offs: fastpass reduces time-to-onboard but requires strict customer-provided proxy hygiene and signed wartime rollback agreement. Engineering may require a short-term patch for the agent to support ephemeral proxy auth tokens.
comm_plan: Publish runbook to Confluence, announce in #customer-onboarding, schedule two training sessions for Solutions Engineering, and add intake form updates to customer portal. Include example comms for failed-stage remediation.
risk_and_mitigations: Risk: Customer proxy misconfiguration leading to partial telemetry — Mitigation: pre-test checklist and mandatory test window with SEs present
Risk: Elevated support load for concierge lane — Mitigation: cap concierge slots per quarter and provide clear eligibility criteria
Risk: Security posture variance across customers — Mitigation: require signed scoping doc and minimum-viable HSM/KMS posture for all concierge/fastpass customers
